data: Blue Origin's two-stage reusable heavy-lift orbital launcher — BE-4 first stage + cryogenic second

Fleet launcher entry backfilled to wire New Glenn up through /plan's view-in-fleet link. First flight = NG-1 from LC-36 (2025-01-16) successfully delivered the Blue Ring pathfinder to orbit; first-stage landing attempt failed but the vehicle was certified for repeat ops. Distinct from New Shepard (Blue Origin's earlier suborbital crew launcher; lives under crewed-spacecraft).
Blue Origin's two-stage reusable heavy-lift orbital launcher

Two-stage heavy-lift vehicle built around seven BE-4 methane engines on the first stage (the same engine Vulcan uses) and two hydrogen-burning BE-3U engines on the second. Designed for first-stage recovery via a downrange ship landing. Lifts ~45 t to LEO and is certified for NSSL Phase 3 + Project Kuiper deployments. Maiden flight NG-1 launched from Cape Canaveral LC-36 on 2025-01-16 and successfully delivered the Blue Ring pathfinder to orbit — the first-stage landing attempt was lost but the orbital insertion was clean.
First flight of Blue Origin's Blue Moon lunar lander architecture
Blue Origin's first-generation lunar cargo lander — single-stage hydrogen / oxygen vehicle, ~3 t to the surface
Replaces H-IIA / H-IIB at lower cost
